subject: Hosted API: data replication, TTL and deletion clarifications
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novuspay.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API: questions on replication and TTL for regulated data

Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — NovusPay's legal/compliance team has a few focused questions about how Redwood handles replication and retention for customer data when using the Hosted API. We're preparing answers for our vendor security questionnaire and hoping for crisp, operational details we can include. A few bullets below — apologies if some are answered in your public docs, but we want explicit responses we can attach to the questionnaire.

1) Cross-region replication: Do you replicate customer data outside of the customer-selected primary region by default? If so, which data classes are replicated (raw request text, embeddings, logs, KV cache)?
2) Snapshots/backups: What's the default snapshot cadence and retention window for backups of tenant data used for disaster recovery? Are backups encrypted separately from live data?
3) Deletion/eradication: If NovusPay requests tenant erasure, what is the operational timeline for removing live copies, replicates, and backups? Please include both typical and maximum timelines.
4) Audit logs & metadata: How long do you keep logs (request traces, routing, audit trail) and are those logs removable on request?
5) Opt-outs/controls: Are there settings to prevent cross-region copies or to force zero retention for model inputs? If so, how are those set (account config, contract, API)?

Attached is our short vendor questionnaire (NovusPay_Security_Qs.pdf). Can you reply by end of week? If it's easier, we're happy to follow with a short call.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior InfoSec Manager
NovusPay
[Attachment: NovusPay_Security_Qs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novuspay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on replication and TTL for regulated data

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Security & Compliance) and Jonas (Solutions) so we can be explicit. Answers below are for the Hosted API default configuration; we can provide addenda for Dedicated/Private if helpful.

1) Cross-region replication
- Default behavior: Tenant data for Hosted API is stored primarily in the customer-selected region and is not proactively replicated outside that region for regulatory data by default.
- Availability replicas: We maintain short-lived read-replicas in nearby regions only when a customer enables cross-region DR/availability. Those replicas are used solely for failover and are not used for analytics or model training.
- Data classes: Live request payloads (model inputs) and derived outputs are stored in the primary region. KV/ephemeral caches are local and flushed per TTL. Audit logs and routing metadata may be routed to a central observability plane but can be configured to be region-scoped (see opt-outs).

2) Snapshots/backups
- Default cadence: incremental snapshots every 24 hours with point-in-time (PIT) snapshots retained for 14 days by default. Full daily snapshots are retained for 14 days; customers can request longer retention (archive options).
- Encryption: All backups are encrypted at rest. If you enable Customer-Managed Keys (CMK), snapshot copies are encrypted with your CMK; otherwise we use our KMS.

3) Deletion/eradication
- Live data: Upon a verified erasure request, live data (active tenant objects and model inputs) are removed from the serving layer within 48 hours.
- Replicas: If cross-region replicas exist, deletion is propagated to replicas within 72 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: Snapshot pruning runs daily; purging the relevant snapshot chain completes within the next scheduled retention sweep (typically within 14 days). For contractually required accelerated purges we offer an expedited deletion workflow (see below).

4) Audit logs & metadata
- Default retention: Operational audit logs (routing, request metadata) retained 90 days by default. These logs are metadata-only (no customer PII payloads). Logs are removable on request; removal requests follow the same verified erasure workflow and metadata purging window of 14 days for associated indices.

5) Opt-outs/controls
- Region lock: Customers may elect a region-lock flag at account provisioning that prevents any automatic cross-region replicas. This is a configuration option we enable from the control plane and can be set in the order form for new accounts.
- Zero-input retention: For sensitive workloads you can enable a policy that prevents persistence of raw model inputs (they remain in memory for inference and are not written to long-term storage). This is an account-level setting; where required we include it in our MSA addendum.

Next steps: attaching a simple diagram and a short attestation template. If this covers it, we can produce a focused attestation and sign-off for NovusPay's questionnaire. Would you like that?

Best,
Markus
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: replication-architecture-diagram.png (image)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novuspay.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-26T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on replication and TTL for regulated data

Tom — adding some operational detail from Compliance so you can paste straight into the vendor sheet.

- Ephemeral caches: KV and prefix caches exist to improve latency; default eviction TTL is 10 minutes and cache entries are encrypted in memory. They are not persisted to backups.
- Backups: We store encrypted PIT snapshots in the primary region by default. Retention = 14 days (default). For customers requiring longer retention (legal hold/archival) we offer a configurable snapshot retention policy up to 7 years under an archival contract.
- Erasure timelines (formal):
  * Acknowledgement of erasure request: within 24 hours of verified request.
  * Live/serving purge: within 48 hours.
  * Replica propagation: within 72 hours if applicable.
  * Snapshot purge: within 14 days; expedited purge available (SLA dependent) — expedited purges may incur a one-time administrative fee.
- Audit logs: metadata-only traces kept 90 days by default; customers who require shorter windows can request 30/7 day windows during onboarding. Complete eradication of audit indices requires a verification step and completes within the snapshot purge window.
- Encryption & keys: By default we manage encryption keys. Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS are supported for Hosted accounts; when CMK is enabled any cross-region replica or snapshot copy is also encrypted under that CMK.

Compliance references:
- Hosted data handling: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/hosted-data-handling
- Data replication diagram: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-replication-diagram

If you want, we can produce a formal, signed attestation and a short contract addendum that locks region-lock and zero-input retention. Markus / Jonas — can you confirm the cost/ops steps for expedited snapshot purge?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novuspay.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on replication and TTL for regulated data

Thanks — that's very helpful and precise. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) For our procurement team we need an explicit attestation PDF that says: "NovusPay tenant data will not be replicated outside the EU unless NovusPay requests cross-region DR and provides written authorization." Can you provide that as a signed PDF?
2) For contract redlines: our legal team will propose a small amendment that requires region-lock by default for EU-paying customers. Can Redwood accept region-lock as a default (technical control + MSA clause) for EU accounts?

If both are yes, procurement will move forward. Appreciate the quick turn.

—Tom
